objective: Apply simultaneous eight-neighbour Life rules to a bounded finite nonwrapping grid using mapped output and fixed offset loops.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Cellular simulations remain a useful current programming exercise.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Neighbourhood transforms arise in grids, games and image processing.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Reading old state while constructing new state prevents ordering dependence.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: ASCII cells and bounded dimensions isolate the intended map/loop skill.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Self-counting, wraparound and in-place transitions produce wrong states.

defects: Junior used imperative growing row strings rather than the requested nested maps; senior used replace/precomputed offsets rather than the requested fixed nested offset loops.
Zero-width rows, frozen ownership and growth dimensions were unstated.
A ten-row cap passed prior small cases.
rationale: Retain the correct reference and align junior/senior to nested row/cell maps and two fixed -1..1 offset loops. Bound rows/width to 100, explicitly allow empty/zero-width/frozen input, require fresh output and define n as rows plus cells so zero-width rows still count. The linear target follows fixed nine-offset checks. Add an independent live-coordinate oracle over all 512 3x3 states, a 100x100 fully alive grid (four surviving corners), unchanged input, fresh empty output and 100 zero-width rows. Gardner’s original rules support the local survival/birth/simultaneity rule; finite cropping/nonwrapping is the task’s explicit boundary model.

State a comparison-sort cost model under bounded depth/name size. Add __proto__/constructor/toString folders, numeric-looking files and Unicode order, 1000 root files, twenty-segment indentation, unchanged input and fresh empty output.

objective: Compare bounded acyclic logical value trees symmetrically using Object.is, dense numeric indices and own enumerable record keys.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Structural comparison remains useful for data contracts.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Nested records and arrays need defined equality beyond identity.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Symmetry, property ownership and sparse iteration semantics generalize.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Explicit supported data/cycle/depth rules avoid claiming universal object equality.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Skipped holes and array extra properties made variants disagree and could violate symmetry.

defects: Reference every skipped holes, so a hole versus a nonundefined item could compare true in one direction only.
Senior compared arrays by enumerable keys without length/index semantics, conflating different sparse lengths and observing extra named properties.
Junior bypassed every; supported keys, cycles, sharing and signed-zero behavior were insufficiently explicit, and a hint overstated Array.isArray as the only reliable distinction.
rationale: All boards compare array lengths and every dense generated index, reading a missing own index as undefined and ignoring extra array properties. Junior uses every for records too. Define own enumerable string record keys, ignored nonenumerable/symbol metadata and default/null prototype differences, read-only acyclic bounded trees and expanded occurrences for shared subtrees. Clarify Object.is signed zeros/NaN and linear expanded-data time with worst-case key/index/stack space. Add hole/value symmetry, hole/undefined equivalence, sparse length mismatch, array metadata, signed zeros/NaN, null-prototype/frozen records, ignored hidden/symbol keys, 10000 entries and depth 100.

objective: Validate dense numerical 9x9 shape and cells, then reject row/column/box duplicates with twenty-seven independent Sets without solving.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Bounded validation and independent Set state remain useful.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Grid validation requires both input-shape and invariant checks.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Dense iteration, value validation and independent accumulators transfer widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A fixed 9x9 board makes the constant-size cost lesson precise.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Wrong types, holes, out-of-range values and shared Sets can admit invalid boards.

defects: Supplied boards checked only lengths and duplicates, accepting some invalid cell values and throwing on malformed outer/row values.
Sparse arrays could skip every shape checks.
Junior used three separate scans and senior one tagged Set rather than the requested two-loop/twenty-seven-Set structure.
rationale: All boards first validate an actual array/own-row shape with every over dense indices, then reject missing own cells and noninteger/out-of-range Numbers before duplicate checks. Align junior/senior to twenty-seven independent Sets and fixed nested loops. Define false for malformed shape/cells, frozen input, ignored unrelated metadata and -0 as empty; preserve that validity does not imply solvability. Explicit O(1) time/space reflects the fixed 81 cells, with invalid larger shapes rejected from length. Add ten invalid value types/ranges, null/string/sparse shapes, complete frozen valid board/immutability, all -0 cells and a locally valid but unsatisfiable partial board.
